nodes.title: Restriction of F-isocrystals to a dense open is fully faithful, and closed under subquotients in the overconvergent case
nodes.statement: Let X be a smooth variety over a perfect field k and U ⊂ X a dense open. (i) The restriction functor F-Isoc(X) → F-Isoc(U) on convergent F-isocrystals is fully faithful. (ii) The restriction functor F-Isoc†(X) → F-Isoc†(U) on overconvergent F-isocrystals is fully faithful, and its essential image is closed under subquotients: every overconvergent sub-F-isocrystal of E|_U is the restriction of a sub-F-isocrystal of E. (iii) More generally, for U smooth dense in X, the restriction F-Isoc†(U, X/K) → F-Isoc(U/K) from isocrystals partially overconvergent along X \ U to convergent ones is fully faithful.
hypotheses: Frobenius structures are needed in (i) and (iii); (ii) holds already without Frobenius (RD.5/extension-across-boundary).
Perfect k as in D'Addezio; Kedlaya's statements allow any k for (ii).
proofSteps: (ii) Full faithfulness and closure under subobjects from RD.5/extension-across-boundary (a), (b), applied to E and to Frobenius pullbacks (Frobenius structures extend by full faithfulness); quotients by duality.

(iii) Kedlaya, Semistable reduction II, Theorem 4.2.1: reduce to Hom(O, E), i.e. Frobenius-invariant horizontal sections; for a smooth pair (X, X \ U) this is Kedlaya's full-faithfulness argument made unconditional by the local full faithfulness RD.3/local-full-faithfulness; in general choose a quasi-resolution f: X_1 → X (an alteration making (U_1, X_1) a smooth pair, SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.4/de-jong-alteration-theorem), lift a section on U_1, descend it over the finite étale locus U' ⊂ U by adjunction for finite étale pushforward (RD.3/finite-etale-pushforward-of-isocrystals), and extend from U' to U by RD.5/extension-across-boundary, checking Frobenius compatibility on U'.

(i) The restrictions of convergent F-isocrystals on X are naturally partially overconvergent along X \ U. By (iii), a convergent Frobenius-compatible morphism on U is a morphism of these partially overconvergent objects; it extends to X by RD.5/extension-across-boundary and the constant monodromy supplied by the existing convergent extensions. Absolute overconvergent-to-convergent full faithfulness alone would not give this relative assertion (D’Addezio, proof of Theorem 4.1.6).
acceptance: For X = A^1, U = G_m and the unit object, underlying isocrystal endomorphisms are K on both opens; endomorphisms respecting σ-semilinear Frobenius are the fixed field K^σ. Both restriction maps are isomorphisms.

On the ordinary locus U of the Legendre family B, R^1f_*O has a unit-root convergent subcrystal on U that is not overconvergent, so the subquotient closure in (ii) fails for the convergent category (Kedlaya, Semistable reduction I, Remark 5.3.2).

nodes.title: Convergent log-isocrystals on a smooth pair
nodes.statement: Let (X, Z) be a smooth pair over k (X smooth, Z a strict normal crossings divisor) with log structure M defined by Z, and suppose given a closed immersion i of X into a formal V-scheme P smooth near X with a log structure L defined by a relative normal crossings divisor lifting Z (Kedlaya's Hypothesis 6.1.6). A convergent log-isocrystal on (X, M) is a coherent module E on the log tube ]X[^log_P with an isomorphism ε: π_2^*E ≅ π_1^*E on the log tube of the diagonal ]X[^log_{P(1)} satisfying Δ^*ε = id and the cocycle condition on ]X[^log_{P(2)}. Equivalently it is a coherent module on the tube with a convergent integrable log connection Ω^1(log) (Kedlaya Theorem 6.4.1); the residues along the components of Z are endomorphisms of the restrictions; a log-F-isocrystal adds a Frobenius isomorphism. The category is independent of i and agrees with Shiho's convergent log-isocrystals.
hypotheses: Smooth pair (X, Z) with Z strict normal crossings.
Frobenius structures where stated.
proofSteps: Log tubes and the log diagonal: Kedlaya Definition 6.1.4 (after Shiho §2.2), with Remark 6.1.5 on existence of the embedding data.
Definition 6.1.7 with Shiho's Proposition 2.2.7 for independence of choices.
Equivalence with convergent log-∇-modules on the tube: Kedlaya Theorem 6.4.1 (via the log Taylor isomorphism).
acceptance: For Z = ∅, convergent log-isocrystals are convergent isocrystals.

For (A^1,{0}), (O,d + a dt/t) with a ∈ Z_p ⊂ K is a convergent log-isocrystal with residue a: its logarithmic Taylor series is (1+u)^a, convergent for |u| < 1. An arbitrary a ∈ K need not be log-convergent.

sources.match: Defines log tubes and convergent log-isocrystals by a stratification on the log tube of the diagonal, independent of the embedding by Shiho's results.

tests.name: convergentLogIsocrystal_residue_computation

tests.name: convergentLogFIsocrystal_nilpotent
tests.statement: A log-F-isocrystal has nilpotent residues: for q-power Frobenius with coefficient action σ, NΦ = qΦσ(N). The characteristic-polynomial coefficients satisfy c_j = q^jσ(c_j); σ is isometric and |q| < 1, so c_j = 0 for j > 0. Linear conjugacy to qN is the special case σ = id.

tests.name: convergentLogIsocrystal_integrable_not_convergent

nodes.title: Logarithmic extension of isocrystals with unipotent monodromy
nodes.statement: Let U ⊂ X be an open immersion of smooth k-varieties with Z = X \ U a strict normal crossings divisor, and E an isocrystal on U overconvergent along Z. Then E has unipotent monodromy along Z iff E extends to a convergent log-isocrystal with nilpotent residues on (X, Z). The restriction functor from convergent log-isocrystals with nilpotent residues on (X, Z) to Isoc†(U, X/K) is fully faithful, so the extension is unique; Frobenius structures extend uniquely, so the same holds for F-isocrystals.
hypotheses: Strict normal crossings boundary; smooth X.
proofSteps: Zariski-local on X; under Hypothesis 6.2.1 the claim combines Kedlaya Proposition 6.3.2 (unipotent ∇-modules near Z are unipotent log-∇-modules, extendable across the tube of Z by Theorem 3.3.4) with Theorem 6.4.1 (log-∇-modules versus convergent log-isocrystals) (Kedlaya Theorem 6.4.5).
Full faithfulness: a horizontal section of a log-∇-module with nilpotent residues on the punctured tube extends across the tube (Theorem 3.3.4: unipotent objects are U_I of their fibre).
Frobenius: the extension of Φ: F^*E ≅ E is the unique extension of a morphism (full faithfulness).
acceptance: For (A^1, {0}) and the unipotent rank-two isocrystal on G_m with ∇ = d + N dt/t, N nilpotent, the extension is the same formula on the disc.
The Kummer isocrystal (O, d + (1/2)dt/t) on G_m is not unipotent along 0; its natural extension to A^1 has residue 1/2, not nilpotent, matching the 'only if'.

sources.match: Unipotent monodromy along an SNC divisor is equivalent to the existence of a convergent log-isocrystal extension with nilpotent residues; restriction is fully faithful.

The functor U_I from modules on the base with commuting nilpotent residues to unipotent log-∇-modules on the base times a polyannulus is an equivalence, which lets a unipotent module extend across the polydisc.
Uses Theorem 6.4.5 of part I to log-extend near the centre of a valuation, with unique extension of the Frobenius structure.

nodes.title: Kedlaya's semistable reduction theorem for overconvergent F-isocrystals
nodes.statement: Let Z ⊂ X be a closed immersion of k-varieties with X \ Z smooth, and E an F-isocrystal on X \ Z overconvergent along Z. Then, after replacing k by k^{q^{−n}} for some n ≥ 0, there is an alteration f: X_1 → X (separable when k is perfect) such that, with Z_1 = (f^{−1}(Z))_red, (X_1, Z_1) is a smooth pair and f^*E extends to a convergent log-F-isocrystal with nilpotent residues on (X_1, Z_1); equivalently f^*E has unipotent monodromy along Z_1. In particular, for X smooth and E ∈ F-Isoc†(X), there is a generically finite alteration X_1 → X from an open X_1 of a smooth proper variety Ȳ_1 with SNC boundary along which f^*E is docile.
hypotheses: Frobenius structure on E (as in the p-adic local monodromy theorem, of which this is the higher-dimensional form).
Alterations in de Jong's sense (proper, surjective, generically finite) from SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.4; the alteration depends on E.
proofSteps: Local semistable reduction at every valuation v of k(X) centred on Z (Kedlaya, Semistable reduction IV, Theorem 2.4.3): reduce to k algebraically closed and v minimal (Semistable reduction III); for transcendence defect 0 (monomial valuations) this is Semistable reduction III, Theorem 6.3.1, built on the p-adic local monodromy theorem over polyannuli (RD.2/quasi-unipotence-and-local-monodromy-statement in relative form); induction on transcendence defect is Semistable reduction IV, Theorem 5.0.1.

Global from local: the locus of valuations where a given alteration achieves semistable reduction is open in the Riemann–Zariski space, which is quasi-compact; finitely many local alterations are combined into one via de Jong's theorem and Galois closures (Semistable reduction II, Propositions 3.3.4 and 3.4.5; Semistable reduction IV, Definition 2.3.10 and Theorem 2.4.4).
Equivalence with unipotent monodromy: RD.5/log-extension-of-unipotent-isocrystal.
acceptance: For X = P^1, Z = {∞} and E the Dwork isocrystal on A^1, the Artin–Schreier alteration P^1 → P^1, t = y^p − y, makes E constant (RD.2/dwork-exponential-artin-schreier-example), hence docile.
For the Kummer isocrystal (O, d + a dt/t) on G_m with a ∈ (q − 1)^{−1}ℤ, the Kummer alteration t = s^{q−1} makes it docile.

sources.match: Defines local semistable reduction at a valuation and proves local and global semistable reduction for F-isocrystals overconvergent along a closed subscheme.

nodes.title: Acceptance: docility of the Kummer and Dwork isocrystals and their semistable reduction
nodes.statement: (1) On G_m ⊂ P^1 over F_q, the Kummer F-isocrystal K_a = (O, d + a dt/t) with a ∈ (q − 1)^{−1}ℤ is docile along {0, ∞} iff a ∈ ℤ; its pullback along the Kummer cover s ↦ s^{q−1} = t is constant, hence docile, and its canonical nilpotent-residue log extension to (P^1, {0, ∞}) after pullback has zero residues. (2) On A^1 ⊂ P^1, the Dwork F-isocrystal L_π is not docile along ∞ (Swan conductor 1), and no tame power cover t = s^m with p ∤ m makes it docile; its pullback along the Artin–Schreier cover y^p − y = t is constant. (3) The restriction to G_m of any docile F-isocrystal on A^1 ⊂ P^1 (docile along ∞) is docile along {0, ∞}, and restriction is fully faithful (RD.5/dense-open-restriction-fully-faithful).
hypotheses: Conventions for L_π as in RD.1/dwork-exponential-module (π^{p−1} = −p).
q = p^f; the Kummer twist uses a ∈ (q − 1)^{−1}ℤ so that a Frobenius structure exists.
proofSteps: (1) Residues: K_a has residue a at 0 and −a at ∞; unipotent rank one means constant, i.e. residue in ℤ after gauge transformation by t^n (RD.2/unipotent-iff-nilpotent-residue); pullback along s^{q−1} multiplies the residue by q − 1.

(2) The Dwork module has highest break 1 at ∞. For a tame power cover x = y^m in a local parameter at ∞, Kedlaya Semistable reduction IV, Lemma 3.1.8 gives f_i(F,s/m)−s/m = f_i(E,s)−s. For a positive break this rescales its slope by m, so the pullback remains nonunipotent. This checks tame power covers specifically; Artin–Schreier trivialisation is RD.2/dwork-exponential-artin-schreier-example.
(3) Unipotence along ∞ is unaffected by removing 0 where the isocrystal is overconvergent and regular (constant monodromy), and RD.5/dense-open-restriction-fully-faithful gives full faithfulness.
acceptance: The residues computed in (1) are ±a and change by integers under gauge transformations.
The break computed in (2) is 1.

requests.need: The calculus of universal cohomological descent on an arbitrary site, after SGA 4 Vbis and Conrad's notes (Zureick-Brown Definition 3.12, Theorems 3.16–3.17, Corollary 3.18): a morphism (or augmented simplicial object) X_• → S is of cohomological descent if id → Rp_*p^* is an isomorphism on D^+(S), universally so if this holds after every base change, and relative to a class of sheaves when only those are tested; (i) coverings, and morphisms with local sections, are universally of cohomological descent; (ii) universal cohomological descent is stable under base change, composition and cancellation (if X → Y → Z is, so is Y → Z), also relative to a sheaf and its pullbacks; (iii) for P the class of morphisms universally of cohomological descent, every P-hypercovering is universally of cohomological descent; (iv) disjoint unions of maps of descent relative to F_i are of descent relative to ⊔F_i. E2/hypercover and E2/bounded-below-hypercover-descent supply the topos-level hypercover descent; (i)–(iv) are not among their statements.

For a projective scheme X over a field with an ample line bundle L: (a) the complement of the zero locus of a section of L is affine; (b) for a closed subscheme D and a finite subscheme Z disjoint from D, some section of a power of L vanishes on D and at no point of Z; (c) n + 1 sections of L without common zero define a finite morphism X → P^n (Kedlaya, More étale covers, Lemmas 3–4). These are the projective-geometry inputs of Kedlaya's finite projections étale off the hyperplane at infinity.

Over a discretely valued (spherically complete) K: (a) Mackey's theorem for semi-complete locally convex spaces V = (V'_c)', with the convex equicontinuous subsets of the dual being the relatively linearly compact convex sets; (b) in a Fréchet space every balanced convex closed bounded linearly compact set lies in the closed convex hull of a null sequence (Crew 2.9); (c) an infinite-dimensional K-Banach space is not reflexive; (d) Montel spaces: for Fréchet–Montel spaces the strong and linearly compact duals coincide. These complete L0/nonarchimedean-hahn-banach, L0/pseudo-polar-duality and L0/barrelled-banach-steinhaus for Crew's strictness criteria; the first pass's restructure proposal moves RD.5's strict-map, Fréchet–Montel transpose and finite-cokernel lemmas to L0 as well. (e) Exactness of the inverse-limit Čech sequence for increasing closed discs with Fréchet section spaces and dense restriction maps (the nonarchimedean analytic Mittag–Leffler argument in Crew, proof of Theorem 7.5, pp. 743–744); dense maps alone do not give the algebraic surjective-transition criterion.
